opportunities.title: EIP-7702 Didn't Pull the Trigger, But It Loaded the Gun: How an Ethereum 'Convenience' Upgrade Turned a Breach Into $2.5B Gone
opportunities.why_now: Fresh reporting shows a specific Ethereum permission feature amplified losses in the largest hack in crypto history, giving a concrete technical villain beyond 'North Korea did it.'

opportunities.title: It Wasn't a Smart Contract Exploit. It Was a Laptop.
opportunities.why_now: Binance is now pointing to a single engineer's compromised laptop and private key misuse as the entry point for a $6.3B breach, undercutting the 'sophisticated attack' narrative.
opportunities.angle: Myth-busting thread/post: contrast the breathless hack coverage with the mundane reality that endpoint security, not cryptography, is still the weakest link — tie to employee opsec habits every exchange user should demand

opportunities.title: Your Hardware Wallet Can Be Backdoored Before It Ships: The Trezor Implant Warning Nobody's Talking About
opportunities.why_now: Trezor just flagged a suspected hardware implant in a Safe 5 unit sold through a third-party reseller (CryptoBilis), a supply-chain attack vector that's far scarier than another exchange hack for self-custody believers.
opportunities.angle: Security-led explainer: how hardware implants work, why buying from unofficial resellers is the real risk, concrete checklist for verifying a cold wallet's authenticity before first use

opportunities.title: Bitcoin Didn't Crash Like 2018 After a Bigger Hack Than Ever — That's the Scariest Part
opportunities.why_now: Decrypt's piece notes BTC held up relatively well despite a record $6.3B theft, which fits directly into the channel's 'already priced' thesis about markets normalizing catastrophic risk.
opportunities.angle: Opinion/analysis piece under the brand's signature lens: argue that resilience to hacks isn't bullish maturity, it's desensitization — the market now prices in theft the way it once priced in volatility

opportunities.title: The Freeze That Won't Stick: Why 'Recovering' $6.3B in Stolen Crypto Is Mostly Theater
opportunities.why_now: Experts are now publicly split on whether Binance's asset freezes will actually claw back stolen funds, as the hacker's BTC haul already exceeds Coinbase's entire treasury — a live test of whether 'freezing' means anything on-chain.
opportunities.angle: Skeptic's explainer: walk through how cross-chain laundering (THORChain, etc.) outran the freeze attempts, and what 'recovery' really means when the money's already gone through a mixer and a DPRK ledger
